stability: Three labeled FILE outputs under micro-workflow/conversation-analysis/{workflow_id}/. Labels and basenames are stable API; the field names and nesting shown in each example are stable API — removing or renaming any is a breaking change requiring a TOOL_VERSION bump and a changelog note here. Anything else under the run prefix (_plan/, records.jsonl) is internal and may change without notice. Raw per-chunk model responses live at each bedrock-inference run's own prefix — the chunk-manifest is the pointer, never a copy.

analysis.description: THE product: merged, coverage-validated topic segments with authoritative timestamps resolved from the transcript by cue id (timestamps never pass through a model) — use for chapters, topic navigation, editorial summaries, downstream indexing

discourse_facts.quote: if he talks, he won't make it to the trial

analysis.notes: start_id/end_id reference the transcript's cue ids; start_time/end_time are resolved from the transcript, never model-emitted. discourse_facts may carry `attribution_overlapped_with` (2026-09-18): the cue falls inside a diarization cross-talk span, so the quote could belong to the listed other voice(s) — recorded ambiguity from suggestive upstream evidence (precision 81% en / 56-69% zh, measured on the development corpus), never a re-attribution. `segments_gap` lists cue-id ranges left uncovered — honest partial coverage on a SUCCEEDED run (partial success IS success); the rerun mechanism is a fresh idempotency_token on analyze_conversation, which re-renders identical records under a NEW inference identity. `content_type_candidates` appears ONLY when chunks disagreed with no strict majority: the deduped candidates, coverage-weight-ordered, with overall_content_type still the top-weighted value — reported, never adjudicated by another inference.

chunk-manifest.description: Full traceability without copying data: the chunk plan (cut tiers, gaps, budgets) and POINTERS to each bedrock-inference run — use to audit any segment back to the exact rendered request and raw model response
chunk-manifest.notes: cut_tier ∈ strong-pause | weak-pause | speaker-change | hard-cut | end. Each inference run's own request.jsonl (exact rendered bytes), response.jsonl and summary.json live at its output_s3_prefix — this manifest is the join.

usage.description: Aggregated cost and token accounting across every chunk inference run (model fallbacks included) — use for spend attribution; each run's own usage_tracking.json has the per-state breakdown
usage.notes: cost_is_complete is false when any run priced incompletely (unpriced model rounds) — check it before quoting the figure, the same discipline as bedrock-inference's own summary.
